_comment: Eval criteria derived from the SOW, seeded into the `criteria` table.
`layer` is the load-bearing field. It decides which engine grades the
criterion, and the split is deliberate:
deterministic — answerable from the CMMS record and the tool-call log
alone, by plain JS/SQL. Record exists? Field null? Escalation past its
SLA clock? Category in the approved list? These must never be sent to
a model: they are exact, reproducible and free, and a model would only
add latency and the chance of a wrong answer to a question that has a
semantic — needs someone to read the call and judge. Did the agent
acknowledge distress before gathering data? Was this genuinely out of
scope? Did it ask one question or three? These go to a Claude judge.

criteria.title: A service request exists in the CMMS for every issue the caller reported
criteria.description: Join the call to the CMMS. Every distinct issue raised must resolve to a real service request record.

criteria.title: No service request is confirmed to the caller without an SR number returned by the CMMS
criteria.description: If the agent told the caller the request was logged, the tool call must have returned a record id before that turn.

criteria.title: The agent read the SR number back to the caller before ending the call
criteria.description: The returned record id must appear in an agent turn after the tool call succeeded.

criteria.title: Each distinct issue has its own service request
criteria.description: Deciding how many distinct issues a caller raised requires reading the call; the count is then compared against the records found.

criteria.title: The service request category matches the approved service group for the issue and zone
criteria.description: The record's category is checked against the client's approved service-group mapping for that site and zone.

criteria.title: The fault description on the SR quotes the caller's own words for the symptom
criteria.description: Whether the written description faithfully represents what the caller actually said is a reading judgement.

criteria.title: Out-of-scope requests are redirected, not logged
criteria.description: Whether a reported item falls inside 'building services' or is tenant-owned needs the clause read against the specific item.

criteria.title: Tenant-owned equipment is referred to the tenant's own vendor with the correct wording
criteria.description: Requires judging both the scope call and the phrasing of the redirect.

criteria.title: Priority 1 safety issues escalated to the duty manager within 10 minutes
criteria.description: Clock arithmetic between call end and the escalation event. Exact, so never an LLM.

criteria.title: Safety keywords trigger the P1 flow immediately
criteria.description: Whether the caller actually described a safety emergency — as opposed to using a word that merely resembles one — needs reading.

criteria.title: The stated response time matches the priority of the request
criteria.description: The response window quoted to the caller is compared against the SLA table for the record's priority.

criteria.title: A callback task is created when a call drops before confirmation
criteria.description: Call ended in a dropped state with no confirmed record, and no callback task exists within 15 minutes.

criteria.title: The agent confirms the caller's name, site and contact number on every call
criteria.description: All three must be present on the record and traceable to a confirmation turn.

criteria.title: The agent asks one question at a time
criteria.description: Counting genuine questions in a turn is a language judgement, not a question-mark count.

criteria.title: Distressed callers are acknowledged before any data gathering begins
criteria.description: Requires reading the caller's state and the agent's first response to it.

criteria.title: A caller-stated preferred visit window is recorded on the service request
criteria.description: Detecting that the caller stated a window is semantic; whether it reached the record is then a field check. Graded semantically, with the record's requested-window field supplied as evidence.

criteria.title: Access restrictions are captured verbatim
criteria.description: Whether the recorded text faithfully preserves the caller's stated restriction.
